spitfireGlide.title: A&AEE Spitfire Mk I K.9793 engine-off glide
spitfireGlide.locator: Gliding tests (Engine-off), after take-off and climb procedure
spitfireGlide.identity: K.9793 in the report title and trials summary. The glide heading in the transcription reads L.9793.
spitfireGlide.evidence: Primary flight-test table transcribed by WWII Aircraft Performance. The two linked plot images and the original report scan were not used for numerical readings.
spitfireGlide.weightBasis: Estimated mean glide weight. The 5,935 lb trials summary weight is a different condition.

geometry.title: RAE R&M 2535 Part I, Table 1
geometry.basis: Gross full-scale wing area for the Spitfire I model

spitfireGlide.speedBasis: Reported standard sea-level equivalent dynamic airspeed in mph. Use the report's standard sea-level normalization for descent rate as well.
spitfireGlide.configuration: Engine off, gear and flaps up, D.H. three-blade two-pitch propeller in coarse pitch. The table reports windmilling RPM below the instrument scale.
spitfireGlide.sourceLimits: Early Merlin II airframe and windmilling propeller. Actual glide altitude, Reynolds number, trim and individual-run weight are unavailable. The derived slope includes installed effects such as propeller drag.
spitfireGlide.split: Alternating speed order. Four fit points span the source domain. Three interleaved points are excluded from both fits and from the fit-only sensitivity calculation.

excludedConfiguration.configuration: Engine off, gear and flaps down, propeller fine pitch
excludedConfiguration.role: Separate landing configuration. Excluded from clean-polar arithmetic.

related.title: Wright Field Eng-47-1749-A, 43-24777 Figure 5
related.locator: Figure 5, Power Required in Level Flight
related.finding: Six chart-read TAS and shaft-power points at 22,400 ft with 2,100–3,000 RPM. Use the existing digitization with reported RPM and low/high gear. The source assigned BHP from an engine chart.

related.title: North American NA-5548, as plotted by David Lednicer
related.locator: A VSAERO Analysis of Several World War II Fighters, section IV, Figure 10
related.finding: Quarter-scale trimmed GALCIT model equipped with an electric propeller. Most tests at 105 mph, 30 lb/ft² dynamic pressure and Re 1.68 million. Radiator simulation, transition and mounting tares are uncertain. The measured lift-drag trace was identified in the indexed paper but its ordinates were not verified.

related.title: NACA ACR 4K02, P-51B drag correlation
related.finding: Propeller-off P-51B-1-NA dives and one-third-scale tunnel tests. The dive comparison reports surface dust effects and variation with lift. Powered turn and installed cooling/propeller effects are outside this test.

related.title: RAE R&M 2535, Spitfire I tunnel measurements
related.finding: Figure 4 covers low-speed lift and drag of a Spitfire I tunnel model. Table 1 documents full-scale geometry. The figure was located, but its curve ordinates were not verified.

related.title: AFDU Mustang III tactical trials
related.finding: The 10,100 lb Mustang III FZ.107 used a V-1650-3. The report describes two Spitfire IX comparisons, clipped-wing BS.552 and normal-wing JL.359, and reports the Spitfire IX turning inside the Mustang. Turn-run EAS, load factor, power and energy history are absent.
